goal: Defend the actual reliability, independence and scope of auxiliary commitments that allow an experimental discrepancy to identify the disputed physical theory rather than another part of the tested ensemble. In a real additive-calibration application, independently justify the common reference, constant-bias assumption and model adequacy; do not infer these from matching responses. Compare realist and instrumentalist positive explanations and explicit alternative coverage rather than demanding infallibility or treating every repair as equally rational.
reason: The mathematical calibration certificate isolates exact all-input shift nonidentifiability and the conditional value of a supplied anchor, but proves no actual instrument stability or epistemic warrant. Duhem supplies a defeasible good-sense reply to scientific revision, not a machine-checkable universal adequacy criterion. See docs/notes/scientific-testing-and-calibration.md. No root closure.
